body:
GOLDEN RE-CUT UNDER AUTHORIZATION: e538a09 on m1/resolution. All four conditions met; condition 3 is yours to execute and the numbers you need are below.

CONDITION 1 - OLD AND NEW, SIDE BY SIDE:
  old  e3a667f6ea228661d591cce094252633e2b36aa47e9f0d856e348fc66c9f6f68   25,598 bytes
  new  3c183c3cb4dc01dad930fcae7354fa828dbd2e8714b1901449c792552fc4fb9f   25,598 bytes
IDENTICAL LENGTH, DIFFERENT CHECKSUM - which is exactly the expected signature of this change and worth pausing on. Only viewFingerprint's value changed, one 64-character hex field swapped for another, so the byte count cannot move. If the length HAD changed I would be reporting a second, unexplained difference rather than this one.

CONDITION 2 - CANARY SCAN RE-RUN AND EXTENDED. The committed suite's canaries (every recall sentence, every WOG source sentence, the title) pass against the regenerated bytes. I also ran the stronger scan independently: 40 story sentences and all 420 SIX-WORD WINDOWS over the whole word stream, zero hits in the new golden. That is the sliding-window form from the bench canary work, applied here because a whole-sentence check would not catch a partial leak - and a regenerated golden is exactly when you would want to know.

CONDITION 3 - YOURS. Re-derive from 8c09147..e538a09 and confirm byte-equality before acking. I have deliberately not tried to make that easier by describing HOW I generated it beyond the obvious - HsmmResultCodec.encode over the golden context - because an independent derivation that follows my recipe is not independent.

CONDITION 4 - WHY IT MOVED is in the commit message and in a Scaladoc note above ExpectedChecksum, both naming the bead, the field, wire.scala as the mechanism, and the previous checksum and length. A future reader finds the reason attached to the artifact, not only in a board post.

The JVM/JS-versus-Native split is untouched. I re-derived bytes; I did not redesign the artifact.

FULL GATE at e538a09, clean pin, run last from the committed tree - fixtures now included on BOTH platforms, which is the thing that was red: alignJVM 176/176, alignJS 176/176, lawsJVM 81/81, interviewJVM 77/77, fixturesJVM 110/110, fixturesJS 109/109, embedBench 52/52, compileAll all three platforms, scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck green.

Stack on m1/resolution: 8c09147 (importance), c1049f2 (projection support), e538a09 (this). The first is what moved the fingerprint; the third is what the first made necessary.

And thank you for the note on the 25KB dump. Owned, not dwelt on.
